NONE: C1 a usually public sale of goods or property, where people make higher and higher bids (= offers of money) for each thing, until the thing is sold to the person who will pay most
› to sell something in a public auction

example: They're holding an auction of jewellery on Thursday.
他們將在週四舉行一場珠寶拍賣會。
The painting will be sold at auction next week.
The house and its contents are being put up for auction.
這座房子及裡面的家當將交付拍賣。
The stamps will be auctioned tomorrow.
這些郵票將在明天拍賣。
The family is auctioning (off) its art collection.
這家人將要拍賣他們的藝術收藏品。

NONE: › a company whose business is selling things at auction

› an occasion when people bid (= offer money and compete against other people) for something that someone has offered to do, for example cook a meal, wash a car, etc. It is usually done in order to get money for a charity.
› a person in charge of an auction who calls out the prices that people offer
